title: Buying an in-the-money call spread can give positive theta
summary: Long options usually lose value with time. An in-the-money call spread is different: the short leg has more theta than the long leg, so the net position earns time decay. The example is a Microsoft 350/380 call spread expiring in April, priced below the intrinsic value of the two legs.

steps.caption: Microsoft trades above both strikes, so the 350/380 call spread is in the money.
Long 350 call, short 380 call, expiring in April.
Net theta is positive here: the short 380 call decays faster than the long 350 call.
Delta is still positive: the trade keeps a bullish tilt.
Gamma is negative near the money: a sharp drop toward the strikes hurts.
Vega is small and negative: a rise in implied volatility costs a little.

takeaways: An ITM call spread can cost less than the intrinsic value of its legs.
The short leg carries more theta, so the spread has positive carry.
You still need the stock to stay above the strikes; the loss is the full debit below the long strike.
caveats: The spot price and implied volatility are estimates; the transcript gives only the strikes and the April expiry.
Not a trade recommendation (the speaker says this too). Reward:risk is low; check the owner's X09 rule.

backtest.note: Two-to-three-month call spread with both strikes in the money; exit near 20% gain on the debit or 60% loss.
